name: Trolling from Ships
description: Rod machines on moving ships tow their rigs behind them.

pages.title: Trolling from Ships
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- Rod Holders and reel drives work on physics **ships**.
- The rig is **towed** behind at its line's length.
- A lure dives and works when the ship's speed suits it.
- Fish bite from the water the ship passes over.

Build the machines into a ship (a [#](7A3C9A)[sub-level](entry://glossary/sub_level)[#](), such as a sailing ship or a surfaced submarine) and set rods in. A rig can't get further from the rod tip than the line it was cast with, so a moving ship tows it.\
\
See [#](2E5AAC)[Building a Ship](entry://flight/ship_building)[#]() and [#](2E5AAC)[Sailing and Boats](entry://ocean/sailing)[#]().

A towed **crankbait** dives to its depth and works between its best speeds: 0.6 to 3 m/s, the Deep Crankbait 0.8 to 3.5 m/s down to 5 m. Too slow or too fast and fish mostly ignore it.\
\
The fish that bite follow the water passed, so trolling spreads its catches instead of fishing out one spot.

The **Fuel Reel Drive** needs no shafts, so it suits boats; a Geared drive works off the ship's own rotation.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Tip:** for tuna and sharks, rig a Heavy Boat Rod with a Big-Game Trolling Reel, Heavy Mono line, a Steel Leader and a Big-Game hook or a Deep Crankbait.

[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Watch out:** machines on a ship fish only while the ship is loaded, so stay aboard. Put a chest or belt beside the machines, or catches hang at the rod tip.\
\
Set the drag before setting the rod in: the machine keeps the rod's own.
